Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Babu Lal Ram,Rachana Singh Hon'ble Rajan Roy,J.
Heard Mr. Sudhir Kumar, learned counsel for the revisionists, leaned AGA for the State and learned counsel for the private-respondents.

By means of this criminal revision the revisionists have challenged the order dated 24.05.2023 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Court No. 3, Budaun in Sessions Case No. 432 of 2022 (State vs. Vijay) arising out of case Crime No. 52 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 (3) IPC and 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Sahaswan, District Budau by which the revisionists herein have been summoned under Section 319 Cr.P.C. as accused who are the parents of the main accused - Vijay who has already been enlarged on bail and against whom the Ramautar And Another vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16940018/
1 trial is proceeding.

entities.label: COURT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of counsel for the revisionists is that for summoning a person under Section 319 Cr.P.C. only a prima facie case is to be established from the evidence led before the Court, not necessarily tested on the anvil of cross-examination as held by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Hardeep Singh vs. State of Punjab; (2014) 3 SCC 92, but, it requires much stronger evidence than mere probability of his complicity.

entities.text: Hardeep Singh vs. State of Punjab; (2014) 3 SCC 92
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Based on the aforesaid decision, it is submitted that in the case at hand the Trial Court has not kept in mind the aforesaid legal position and routinely and mechanically summoned the revisionists who are parents and did not have any role to play and they have been roped in subsequently only to harass the family.

Learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 as also learned AGA have opposed the revision on the ground that the summoning order has been passed on the statement of the victim herself who has been cross-examined, therefore, what better evidence could have been led at least at the stage of Section 319 Cr.P.C. for summoning the accused.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the records, I find merit in the submission of counsel for the respondents.

The testimony of the victim PW-1 has been recorded wherein she has made allegations against the revisionists herein also of having participated in commission of the offence which has been mentioned in the order of the Trial Court.

Even after taking into consideration the decision of Honb'le the Supreme Court in the case of Hardeep Singh (supra) and other decisions referred by the Trial Court, this Court is of the opinion that the order of the Trial Court does not suffer from any error and is based on the evidence received by the Trial Court during trial and it cannot be said that the Trial Court has erred in exercising its jurisdiction or it has committed any manifest error so as to require interference exercising revisional jurisdiction by this court.

This, of course, is without prejudice to the rights of the revisionists in the pending trial and the observations made hereinabove will have no bearing on the merits/issues involved nor the admissibility and reliability of the evidence.
Subject to above, the criminal revision is dismissed.

Order Date :- 15.2.2024 Santosh/-
